subject: cross-platform verification in CI

localPosix.where: WSL Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.23.4, pnpm 11.28.0, fresh clone at 6b26aab

theFinding.summary: The GitHub Windows runner reports 7 of the local Windows 15, because it can create symlinks.
whichOnesPass: image route opens nothing but a well-formed id of an intact regular file below the store
workspace images refuses paths that leave the workspace, lexically or through a symlink
card storage keeps the style a card was created with when it is patched after the setting changed
card storage never reads a file outside the store with its own fs
legacy workspace cards refuses a symlink inside the workspace that points out of it
style files route refuses a style file that is a symlink, for reads and writes
style files route refuses a workspace whose .dsh directory links out of it
visualizeTool description names an on-disk contract for agents that cannot load skills
theFinding.whyItMatters: Six of the eight are the symlink containment tests that docs/testing/PLATFORM-FAILURES.md recorded as unprovable on a stock Windows machine. In CI they execute and pass, so the containment check is measured on Windows rather than only read.

crossPlatform.verdict: PLATFORM-SPECIFIC: every locally-failing test passes on POSIX; POSIX is clean

buildReproducibility.note: the bundle does not depend on the platform that built it; CI asserts the same thing on every run

designErrorsFoundAndFixed: the first CI gate compared Linux against the Windows baseline, so a clean platform failed for being clean
the Windows leg died before reaching its gate because vitest exits non-zero on the known failures; the exit code was doing the gating instead of the assertion
the gate then failed when baseline failures started passing, which punished a better runner; now only NEW failures fail it
